Cached data before a collision rollback can be read as committed
Description: There is a race-condition between a collision rollback and MongoDocumentStore's nodesCache leaking uncommitted data, that later gets treated as if committed. Under normal circumstances, a collision is properly cleaned up via a rollback : all colliding data written is removed, and the revision was never marked as committed in the first place. Without the revision marked as committed, no-one would know of that revision - i.e. it wouldn't be able to be read since that clusterId doesn't update parent's lastRevs etc. Subsequent updates on involved documents result in caches to be updated accordingly, after which all traces from a collision rollback are gone. But if a peer cluster manages to read and cache uncommitted data, that later is rolled back due to a collision, it can happen that it treats that data as if committed. This situation only persists as long as that process is running - since this is dependent on cached data. The data in the physical repository is always consistent. So a restart will cause that uncommitted data to disappear again.

title: Keep only traversed state, remove all other revisions
Description: As a slightly different algorithm to OAK-10535 this ticket suggests to calculate the traversedState of a node, then keeps only those revisions needed for that traversedState and removes all others. The main difference is an inversion of logic, where instead of analysing for each revision whether it must be kept or not - this first derives the revision that must be "kept" from the traversedState - then deletes all others. This mechanism applies to all (normal and bundled) properties as well as some DocumentNodeStore internal ones, such as "_deleted". Below are a list of assumptions to back this: * DetailedGC runs only up to the older between the oldest checkpoint and maxRevisionAge (24h by default). Thus a document analysed by DetailedGC is guaranteed to have only 1 revision (per property) that must be kept - as it is guaranteed to not have modifications (revisions) younger than any checkpoint or maxRevisionAge (24h) * To find out which revision(s) must be kept, the node tree is traversed from root (based on current head revision) to the target document. * Given the first bullet (that we're only looking at nodes that have only 1 revision (each, per property) to keep, this traversed node state thus contains the values of those. * Hence, based on each of the property key of the traversed state, the corresponding "commit revision" in the document-local map must be calculated. That local map entry must be kept - all others can be deleted. * Note that this also cleans up overwritten branch commits of the same branch (as only the last, relevant one is kept) As a result of the above, certain other entries can be deleted, namely: * any "_commitRoot" entry no longer referenced by the local document * any "_bc" entry no longer referenced by the local document Independent of the traversedState and the outcome of the cleanup what can also be removed is: * any "_revisions" entry older than the current sweepRev However: "_revisions" entry that might not be referenced by the local document and are younger than the sweepRev must still be kept, as they might be referenced by child documents (through their "_commitRoot" pointing to the current document). Without checking for children and double-checking the actual use, there could as a result still be some garbage "_revisions" entries left.

CachedPrincipalMembershipReader could return empty principal under concurrency
Description: CachedPrincipalMembershipReader can be configured to define a stale time during which an outdated principal list is returned while the cache is being refreshed. If a stale time is configured then there will be a period when the cache it's being updated by one request thread ([here|https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit-oak/blob/9ca692077b7a8c3f43f42895a4c3ba93d0614011/oak-core/src/main/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/oak/security/user/CachedPrincipalMembershipReader.java#L128-L131]) and others request could serve an empty list of principals because the property that contains [the cached principal list is not written yet|https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit-oak/blob/9ca692077b7a8c3f43f42895a4c3ba93d0614011/oak-core/src/main/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/oak/security/user/CachedPrincipalMembershipReader.java#L180-L191]. This can happens depending on the concurrency level and the time it takes to build the principal list from one thread. Also that could happen only if the property is not present which could only occur the first time the cache is being built as the property is not being deleted afterwards.

Resolving a node with an unmerged or not-yet-visible revision as the only revision results in previous document scan (which can be expensive on root)
Description: Consider a scenario with 2 cluster nodes (running DocumentNodeStore): * cluster node A with cluster node id 1 * cluster node B with cluster node id 2 Now cluster node A is doing a merge that includes changes (eg a property) on root. Such a merge includes two updates towards DocumentStore (followed by background stuff) : * the first update has the actual changes on the properties (that would include any other document other than root - but that's not so relevant here). Say that happens with revision {{"rn-0-1"}} * the second update is marking the revision as committed - which is done by adding an entry to "_revisions" with {{"rn-0-1" : "c"}} * after the merge, the usual backgroundWrite(on A)/backgroundRead(on B) will follow. At some point cluster node B reads the root node and does a getNodeAtRevision. The behavior slightly differs between the two cases: * after step 1 it will read {{"rn-0-1"}} in an unmerged state (it has no commit value yet) * after step 2 it will read the revision in a not yet visible state Either way this revision value resolves to null. As a result of which it greedily reads through previous documents to *find a split-away property value* only to find nothing. If there are many previous documents, which is likely on root, this is a significant performance hit. This situation persists until a full backgroundWrite/Read are done, so until step 3 above is done. Now backgroundRead requires the exclusive lock on the backgroundOperationLock as part of updating a fresh main root. If B happens to have that exclusive lock occupied by anyone else, it has to wait. As part of a regular merge though, the "read/non-exclusive" lock of backgroundOperationLock is acquired. If there are a number of threads "ahead" of backgroundRead all acquiring the read-lock of backgroundOperationLock, the backgroundRead will have to wait until all commits are done. So if B is in such a situation, with all merge operations when updating root going through previous documents, it can result in an overall significant delay. (This issue can also happen on any other node - but it is only a problem if there are many previous documents. And root usually does have many, hence the problem is primarily on root)

title: Introduce config for perflogger to log very slow operations at info
Description: In oak we have a [PerfLogger|https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit-oak/blob/trunk/oak-commons/src/main/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/oak/commons/PerfLogger.java#L48] which can be used to log slow operations. It is used in a variety of places, most prominent: * DocumentNodeStore * MongoDocumentStore * EventGenerator * DocumentNodeStoreBranch * AbstractDocumentNodeState * NodeObserver * and in several places in indexing code * as well as in RDB case Currently we use only the DEBUG thresholds, we're not using the INFO thresholds. That means, we only would see logs when the level is at DEBUG, we see nothing by default at INFO. We could however consider logging very slow operations at INFO by default. Much like mongo logs requests slower than 100ms always, by default. In AEM's case we might have many slow operations though, so choosing a low threshold would potentially flood the log and cause troubles that way. Additionally, there isn't a (global) config that can be tweaked to set this threshold. So far it is all hard-coded - and the threshold is actually Long.MAX_VALUE (so essentially never). Suggesting hereby to introduce such a config - perhaps it doens't have to be global, it could be for example covering a few classes. But having such a config, then having that tweakable via skyline-ops, could be a useful feature. We could then set for example a threshold of 60 seconds and monitor the amount of logs generated by that throughout Skyline. If the number is low enough, we can go lower to eg 30 sec or ideally eventually 10 sec. Always given we are not flooding splunk that way. But the prerequisite for something like that is. a skyline-ops configurable perflogger threshold (and wire that to the corresponding {{Perflogger.end()}} methods at places we want it to be.

title: Membership cache fails to update changes on cached properties
Description: Multiple instances of the membership providers using the PrincipalMembershipCacheReader class could lead to do not reflect membership changes properly in the cached properties. Cached properties are managed by PrincipalMembershipCacheReader that keeps track of the expiration date based on the UserConfiguration values. This expiration time is updated every time a property is updated but further updates are not allowed until the cache is expired. When the membership cache is shared among different membership providers could happens that the updates of a provider prevents the changes in membership from a different provider are not updated, depending which provider was the first one to write into the cache.

I have a patch that detects and removes such properties. Until the root cause is fixed, I think it makes sense to use this additional logic.

Vulnerabilities This artifact embeds +zookeeper:3.9.2+ which contain the following vulnerabilities: * *CVE-2024-51504* - When using IPAuthenticationProvider in ZooKeeper Admin Server there is a possibility of Authentication Bypass by Spoofing – this only impacts IP based authentication implemented in ZooKeeper Admin Server. Default configuration of client's IP address detection in IPAuthenticationProvider, which uses HTTP request headers, is weak and allows an attacker to bypass authentication via spoofing client's IP address in request headers. Default configuration honors X-Forwarded-For HTTP header to read client's IP address. X-Forwarded-For request header is mainly used by proxy servers to identify the client and can be easily spoofed by an attacker pretending that the request comes from a different IP address. Admin Server commands, such as snapshot and restore arbitrarily can be executed on successful exploitation which could potentially lead to information leakage or service availability issues. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.9.3, which fixes this issue. h3. Recommendation Apply one of the following suggestions: * Remove usage and dependency * Upgrade to a vulnerability free version of the embedded library. If none is available, upgrade to a less vulnerable version (lower CVSS Score)

DataStore FileCache Memory Usage
Description: If there are many small files in the datastore cache, then the FileCache can use a lot of Java heap memory. This is caused by: * Entries smaller than 4096 bytes report memory usage of 0 to the cache. * Each entry is a java.io.File, which contains the full path. This can lead eg. to 1 GB of memory usage if there are many small files, which is unexpected. To reduce memory usage, I think it makes sense to use just the String as the key as well as the value. It will still not fully resolve the issue, but at least it reduces the memory usage. Better yet would probably be to limit the memory usage as well.

title: XML import: calculate prefixMap only when required
Description: I was tracing an import of a long-running installation of a filevault package and found that {{TargetImportHandler.createCurrentPrefixMap}} is invoked whenever {{startPrefixMapping}} or {{endPrefixMapping}} is invoked. Now I have in the [ImportHandler.startElement|https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit-oak/blob/298ee403db0e1aa40368681e98ee17327bacdb1b/oak-jcr/src/main/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/oak/jcr/xml/ImportHandler.java#L174-L176] TargetImportHandler.startPrefixMapping is invoked in a loop, but next to adding the prefix also the {{currentPrefixMapping}} is calculated; which is not required, as it is only used in {{TargetImportHandler.currentNamePathMapper()}}, which is not called as part of this loop. For that reason the call to {{createCurrentPrefixMap}} should be moved into the {{TargetImportHandler.currentNamePathMapper()}} and only executed when it is actually needed. In my tests this shows up in about 12% of the stacktraces I created during the package import.

refactor parallel compaction inheritance
Description: In preparation for OAK-11895, I would like to refactor the setup for parallel compaction. Currently the {{ParallelCompactor}} extends {{CheckpointCompactor}}, and {{CheckpointCompactor}} delegates to {{ClassicCompactor}}. The fix for OAK-11895 affects {{CheckpointCompactor}}, however, as compaction is a sensitive area in the code, I want to keep the current implementation in {{LegacyCheckpointCompactor}} to allow toggling between the old implementation and the fixed implementation. With {{ParallelCompactor}} extending from {{CheckpointCompactor}}, this would require copying {{ParallelCompactor}} as well. However, if we refactor {{ParallelCompactor}} to extend from {{ClassicCompactor}} instead, then we can pass either a {{ClassicCompactor}} instance or a {{ParallelCompactor}} instance into the constructor of {{CheckpointCompactor}}, and later {{LegacyCheckpointCompactor}}), effectively configuring them to run either single-threaded or in parallel. This avoids the need for duplication of the {{ParallelCompactor}} class when addressing OAK-11895.

title: CheckpointCompactor writes to "after" instead of "onto" NodeState

Likely, this went unnoticed until now, because AFAICS all used invocations within Oak pass the same NodeState for the "after" and "onto" NodeStates. I am trying to create a compacted copy of a segmentstore. In this scenario the "after" NodeState is backed by a {{ReadOnlyFileStore}}, because it is compacting the segmentstore of a running system. When testing this scenario, I got an exception, because the write to the "after" NodeState were denied.

XPath with "or" conditions should not always be converted to "union"
Description: In OAK-1432, XPath queries with "or" conditions are always converted to "union" queries. There are some queries that do not benefit from this forced conversion to "union", for example queries that use elasticsearch indexes for both parts, but where one of the properties is not indexed. In general, it would be better to compare the cost of the union with the cost of the non-union query, and then pick the one with the lower cost. In fact, for SQL-2 queries with "or" conditions, that is how it's working since OAK-1617. It's a bit dangerous now (after such a long time) to always disable the forced "union" conversion for XPath queries. But, what we could do is disable the forced conversion using a feature toggle.

title: Simplified index management
Description: Currently, Oak indexes are defined using JCR nodes. There are a few known issues with the current configuration: * Index definitions can be changed while they are being used. * For Lucene indexes, there are two versions of the index definition: the one visible and in the one used for queries (the so-called "stored" definition). Only setting "reindex" or "refresh" to true updates the stored one. * There can be multiple sources for index definitions: (a) so-called "product" indexes, (b) customizations, and (c) changes via UI or automation. All these sources can be changed independently. It would be good to merge the changes if one of them changes. * Index definitions are JCR nodes, making it hard to change. Using JSON config files would simplify changes (one JSON file per index, or even one JSON file for multiple indexes). * Index definitions are mutable. It would be better if they are effectively immutable, by using versions. I'm proposing to retain the current index configuration, but to add a way to customize indexes via JSON. So that the current configurations are fully backward compatible, but we use a new, additional way to configure indexes.

Offline Compaction does not persist compacted head into gc.log
Description: *Root Cause* The offline compaction in *Compact.run()* calls *compactFull()* and *cleanup()* as two separate calls, but the _CompactionResult_ from compaction is silently discarded between them. *Call chain:* Compact.run() ├─ store.compactFull() │ └─ garbageCollector.compactFull(strategy).isSuccess() │ ^^^^^^^^^^^ │ CompactionResult.succeeded(...) is returned but thrown away! │ └─ store.cleanup() └─ garbageCollector.cleanup(strategy) └─ strategy.cleanup(context) ← no-arg overload └─ AbstractGarbageCollectionStrategy.cleanup(Context): return cleanup(context, CompactionResult.skipped(...)) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Always creates a SKIPPED result! Why *gc.log* is never written: In *AbstractGarbageCollectionStrategy.java:88–95:* // Standalone cleanup always creates a SKIPPED result {code:java} public List<String> cleanup(Context context) throws IOException { return cleanup(context, CompactionResult.skipped(...)); }{code} *CompactionResult.skipped(...)* inherits *requiresGCJournalEntry()* from the base class, which returns false (line 216). Then in *newCleanupStrategyContext()* at line 295–297: {code:java} public GCJournal getGCJournal() { return compactionResult.requiresGCJournalEntry() ? context.getGCJournal() : null; // ↑ false for skipped → returns null! }{code} *DefaultCleanupStrategy* receives null for gcJournal, so it skips the gcJournal.persist(...) call entirely. Contrast with online (integrated) GC: The *AbstractGarbageCollectionStrategy.run()* method calls *cleanup(context, compactionResult)* with the actual *CompactionResult.succeeded(...)* — that's why gc.log works online but not offline.

Cost estimation should be lower if more conditions are indexed
Description: Currently, the cost estimation of the Lucene and Elasticsearch indexes only tracks the minimum across all properties. The number of indexed properties is not taken into account. What should happen is: the more indexed conditions are added to a query, the lower the expected cost should be. Eg. a query with "color = 'red' and id = 1" should have a lower expected cost than a query with just "id = 1" or just "color = 'red'".

title: run S3/GCP integration tests with S3Mock emulator in CI
Description: h2. Summary Integration tests in \{{oak-blob-cloud}} require real AWS or GCP credentials (\{{aws.properties}}) and are skipped in Apache CI because secrets cannot be committed. This issue adds a local S3 emulator (Adobe S3Mock via Testcontainers) so existing integration tests run in CI without cloud credentials, in both *S3* and *GCP* storage modes. h2. Background * Most \{{oak-blob-cloud}} integration tests gate on \{{S3DataStoreUtils.isS3Configured()}} and skip when \{{accessKey}}/\{{secretKey}} are empty. * Azure blob tests already use \{{AzuriteDockerRule}} + Testcontainers (\{{oak-blob-cloud-azure}}) — same pattern, no secrets in CI. * AWS does not provide an official S3 emulator (unlike Azurite for Azure). * Oak *GCP mode* uses the AWS S3 SDK against GCS S3 interoperability — not the native GCS client — so an S3-compatible emulator covers both modes with different config. * Detailed implementation plan: \{{oak-blob-cloud/docs/S3-GCP-EMULATOR-TESTS-PLAN.md}} h2. Proposed solution # Add Adobe S3Mock 5.x (\{{com.adobe.testing:s3mock-testcontainers}}) + Testcontainers to \{{oak-blob-cloud}}. # Introduce \{{S3MockRule}} and \{{S3EmulatorSupport}} (mirror \{{AzuriteDockerRule}}): lazy-start Docker container, skip tests if Docker unavailable. # Wire emulator config into \{{S3DataStoreUtils.getS3Config()}}: #* Real credentials in \{{aws.properties}} / \{{-Ds3.config}} take precedence (manual cloud testing unchanged). #* Otherwise use emulator properties when S3Mock is available. # Run existing test classes in *both* modes via two Maven Surefire executions (\{{-Ds3.test.mode=S3}} and \{{-Ds3.test.mode=GCP}}) — no duplicate test classes. # Small production change: opt-in \{{pathStyleAccess}} property (default \{{false}}) for S3Mock path-style URLs; GCP mode already enables path-style. # Test-only fix: support \{{http://}} presigned URLs in \{{S3DataStoreUtils.getHttpsConnection()}} for direct-access tests. h2. Test tiers (after change) || Tier || When || Purpose || | Unit | Always | Mock/no-network tests (unchanged) | | Emulator | CI / local Docker, no creds | S3Mock — S3 and GCP mode | | Real cloud | Populated \{{aws.properties}} | Optional manual validation | h2. Scope *In scope:* * \{{TestS3Ds}} and subclasses (cache, small cache) * \{{TestS3DataStore}} * \{{S3DataRecordAccessProviderTest}} / \{{S3DataRecordAccessProviderIT}} * \{{S3DataStoreServiceTest}} * SSE subclasses: triage; KMS-with-key / SSE-C remain cloud-only via existing skip logic *Out of scope:* * \{{oak-it}}, \{{oak-jcr}}, \{{oak-upgrade}} S3 tests * Migrating \{{oak-segment-aws}} findify S3Mock to Adobe S3Mock * fake-gcs-server / native GCS client testing h2. Acceptance criteria * \{{mvn test -pl oak-blob-cloud}} passes with Docker and *no* cloud credentials. * Integration tests that currently skip run under the emulator (S3 mode). * Same tests run again under GCP mode (second Surefire execution). * Populated real \{{aws.properties}} still takes precedence. * No secrets in repo or CI. * Production behavior unchanged unless \{{pathStyleAccess=true}} is explicitly set. * Unit tests pass without Docker. h2. References * Azure precedent: \{{oak-blob-cloud-azure/.../AzuriteDockerRule.java}} * S3Mock: https://github.com/adobe/S3Mock * Plan doc: \{{oak-blob-cloud/docs/S3-GCP-EMULATOR-TESTS-PLAN.md}}

oak-http: OakServlet mis-parses HTTP Basic credentials - passwords containing a colon are silently truncated and malformed headers cause an HTTP 500
Description: h2. Description {{OakServlet}} authenticates incoming HTTP requests by decoding the {{Authorization: Basic <base64>}} header and parsing the decoded {{user-id:password}} string. The current implementation is: {code:java} String authorization = request.getHeader("Authorization"); if (authorization != null && authorization.startsWith("Basic ")) { String[] basic = Base64.decode(authorization.substring("Basic ".length())).split(":"); credentials = new SimpleCredentials(basic[0], basic[1].toCharArray()); } else { throw new LoginException(); } {code} (File: {{{}oak-http/src/main/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/oak/http/OakServlet.java{}}}, inside {{{}service(...){}}}.) This violates [RFC 7617|https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7617] ("The 'Basic' HTTP Authentication Scheme"), which states that the credentials are the concatenation of the user-id, a single colon ({{{}:{}}}) character, and the password. The user-id _must not_ contain a colon, but the password _may_ contain any character, including colons. Therefore everything after the *first* colon is the password. Two distinct defects result from using {{String.split(":")}} with no limit: h3. 1. Password truncation / weakened authentication (CWE-287) {{split(":")}} splits on *every* colon and the code keeps only element {{{}[1]{}}}. A password that contains one or more colons is therefore silently truncated to the substring between the first and second colon. The repository then authenticates the user against this shortened secret. *Example:* a user whose password is {{p4ss:w0rd:!}} is authenticated using only {{p4ss}} (the substring between the first and second colon). The effective secret the server verifies is shorter than the one the user actually set, reducing the keyspace an attacker must search and breaking the user's expectation about password strength. h3. 2. Unhandled exception -> HTTP 500 (instead of 401) If the decoded value contains no colon (e.g. a client sends just a user-id, or an empty password {{user:}} - {{String.split}} drops trailing empty strings), accessing {{basic[1]}} throws {{{}ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException{}}}. This runtime exception is *not* caught by the surrounding handlers (which only catch {{LoginException}} and {{{}NoSuchWorkspaceException{}}}), so it escapes as an HTTP 500 with a stack trace rather than a proper 401 Unauthorized challenge. h2. Steps to reproduce *Defect 1 (password truncation):* # Create a user whose password contains a colon, e.g. {{{}p4ss:w0rd:!{}}}. # Send a request with: {{Authorization: Basic <base64 of "user:p4ss:w0rd:!">}} # Observe that authentication is evaluated against {{{}p4ss{}}}, not the full password. A login that should fail with the wrong password can succeed, and the full password is never the one actually checked. *Defect 2 (HTTP 500):* # Send a request with an Authorization header whose decoded value has no colon, e.g. Base64 of {{{}nocolon{}}}: {{Authorization: Basic bm9jb2xvbg==}} # Observe an HTTP 500 ({{{}ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException{}}}) instead of a clean 401 Unauthorized. h2. Expected behaviour * The password is taken as everything after the first colon, preserving any colons it contains (RFC 7617 compliant). * A missing/empty/non-Basic Authorization header, or a decoded value with no colon, results in a 401 Unauthorized challenge - never an HTTP 500. h2. Actual behaviour * Passwords containing colons are truncated at the first colon, weakening authentication. * A decoded value without a colon yields HTTP 500 ({{{}ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException{}}}) instead of 401. h2. Impact * *Security:* effective passwords are silently weakened whenever they contain a colon; the secret actually verified is shorter than the one configured. * *Robustness/availability:* malformed credential headers produce 500 errors and leak a stack trace instead of returning a standard 401 challenge. h2. Proposed fix Split only on the first colon ({{{}indexOf(':'){}}} + {{{}substring{}}}), reject a missing colon with a {{LoginException}} (mapped to 401 by the existing handler), and reject a missing/non-Basic header the same way. The credential parsing could be extracted into a small private helper for clarity, for example: {code:java} private Credentials parseBasicCredentials(String authorization) throws LoginException { if (authorization == null || !authorization.startsWith("Basic ")) { throw new LoginException( "Missing or unsupported Authorization header; expected Basic scheme"); } String decoded = Base64.decode(authorization.substring("Basic ".length())); int colon = decoded.indexOf(':'); if (colon < 0) { throw new LoginException( "Malformed Basic credentials: missing ':' separator"); } String userId = decoded.substring(0, colon); String password = decoded.substring(colon + 1); return new SimpleCredentials(userId, password.toCharArray()); } {code} This is a contained bug fix with no API change, so no feature toggle is required.

Flacky test TokenCleanupTest#testBatchSizeLimitsCleanup
Description: In [https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit-oak/blob/03499ab99de715f054b3ed0e9787c928d9fb2858/oak-core/src/test/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/oak/security/authentication/token/TokenCleanupTest.java#L100] {code:java} org.apache.jackrabbit.oak.security.authentication.token.TokenCleanupTest#testBatchSizeLimitsCleanup{code} TokenProviderImpl.cleanupExpired runs opportunistically on every createToken call whenever shouldRunCleanup(token) is true (~1/8 random chance). In the test, the cleanup threshold (5) equaled the number of expired tokens created, so the 5th expired-token creation could randomly trigger an extra cleanup batch. When that happened, two batches ran and all 5 expired tokens were removed instead of only batchSize (3), producing the intermittent failure. The fix would be to raise the cleanup threshold to expiredCount + 1 so cleanup can never fire during the expired-token creation phase, guaranteeing exactly one cleanup batch during the extras loop. This makes the batch-size assertion deterministic.

Simplified index management improvements
Description: There are various changes and improvements needed for simplified index management: (a) Prevent that migrating to simplified index management disables an index. If indexes were configured previously with version numbers (abc-1-custom-1), but now are migrated to simplified index management, then and then migrated to simplified, there were cases where the old and new version exactly match, and so no new index was created. Because the old one was then no longer active, in reality migration caused a gap (the index definition was still there, but the index is not active). For this, we need to ignore disabled indexes. (b) Support for empty nodes. Currently, empty nodes (without any property) will get "type": "disabled". There is a workaround: set a primary type. But this is ugly. (c) There was some code that in theory could result in null-pointer exceptions in theory. It makes sense to protect against this. (d) It should be allowed to overwrite the facets property "secure".

title: Online revision cleanup can delete referenced segments on a store not written in compaction order (e.g. a promoted cold standby)
Description: {{DefaultCleanupContext.isDanglingFutureSegment}} detects unused (aborted-compaction) segments by scan position: during cleanup, TAR entries are marked newest-first and every compacted segment is treated as reclaimable until the last compacted root recorded in {{gc.log}} is reached (the {{aheadOfRoot}} flag). This assumes segments are physically laid out in compaction write order (the compacted root written last). That assumption does not hold for a segment store assembled out of compaction order — e.g. a cold standby, whose segments are written via {{FileStore.writeSegment}} in sync-arrival order. There the recorded compacted root is not the newest segment, so the reverse scan reaches live, head-referenced compacted segments while {{aheadOfRoot}} is still true and marks them reclaimable. Online revision cleanup then removes referenced segments, and a subsequent read/compaction fails with {{SegmentNotFoundException}}. h4. Steps to reproduce # Promote a cold standby to primary (its segment store was assembled via standby sync). # Run online (full) revision cleanup. Cleanup removes still-referenced compacted segments; the following compaction throws {{SegmentNotFoundException}} while traversing the head. {{oak-run check}} passes immediately before cleanup. h4. Suggested fix Make the dangling-segment test generation-based rather than positional: treat a compacted segment as an unused future segment only if its generation is strictly newer than the head generation. This is independent of physical segment write order and consistent for all store types.

title: Create a Workaround for COLLECTIONS-900 in IteratorUtils
Standalone cleanup() never journals gc.log leading to SNFE on cold standby / backup
Description: {{AbstractGarbageCollectionStrategy.cleanup(Context)}} can run without a preceding local compaction (e.g. {{StandbyClientSync}} after sync, {{{}FileStoreBackupImpl{}}}/{{{}FileStoreBackupRestoreMBean{}}}). In that case it builds a placeholder via {{{}CompactionResult.skipped(...){}}}, whose {{requiresGCJournalEntry()}} is hard-coded to {{{}false{}}}: {code:java} static CompactionResult skipped(...) { return new CompactionResult(currentGeneration, gcCount) { // requiresGCJournalEntry() not overridden -> always false }; } {code} So {{GCJournal.persist(...)}} is never called for this path, even though the reclaimer *is* actively removing segments from older generations. On a cold standby, {{currentGeneration}} legitimately advances on every synced generation, but {{gc.log}} stays frozen and keeps pointing at a stale, already-superseded root. h3. Impact * Standby's own {{gc.log}} never gains new entries after boot, even though sync + cleanup keep reclaiming segments from newer generations. * After promoting the standby to primary, later compaction/cleanup cycles trust this stale {{gc.log}} entry, and reads of already-reclaimed segments throw {{{}SegmentNotFoundException{}}}. * Same exposure via the always-registered {{FileStoreBackupRestoreMBean}} on *any* live instance. h3. Steps to reproduce # Set up primary + cold standby. # Run several rounds of content + online cleanup on primary so multiple generations/gc.log entries exist. # Let standby sync + auto-cleanup after each round. # Standby's {{segmentstore/gc.log}} shows no new entries despite "cleanup completed... space reclaimed" logs and on-disk generation clearly advancing. # Promote standby to primary, keep running cleanup — eventually {{SegmentNotFoundException}} on segments already reclaimed while {{gc.log}} was frozen. h3. Suggested fix {code:java} @Override boolean requiresGCJournalEntry() { return currentGeneration.isCompacted(); } {code} * {{GCJournal.persist}} already no-ops when the generation is unchanged, so this can't cause duplicate/bloated entries. * Fresh, never-compacted repos are unaffected ({{{}isCompacted(){}}} is false at generation 0). * {{{}succeeded(){}}}/{{{}aborted(){}}} paths untouched. * Verified experimentally: previously 100%-reproducible SNFE after standby promotion dropped to 0 occurrences across repeated cycles with this change, and standby {{gc.log}} correctly advanced after every sync+cleanup round.

title: MapEntry.compareTo() allocates a new Comparator chain on every call, adding GC pressure during segment map writes
Description: h2. Summary {{MapEntry.compareTo()}} in oak-segment-tar builds a brand-new {{Comparator}} chain (3 allocated objects: {{comparingLong}} + {{thenComparing}} + a {{Comparator.nullsLast(Comparator.naturalOrder())}} wrapper) on {*}every single pairwise comparison{*}, instead of building it once and reusing it. {code:java} // oak-segment-tar/src/main/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/oak/segment/MapEntry.java:150-155 @Override public int compareTo(@NotNull MapEntry that) { return Comparator.comparingLong((MapEntry me) -> me.getHash() & HASH_MASK) .thenComparing(MapEntry::getName) .thenComparing(MapEntry::getValue, Comparator.nullsLast(Comparator.naturalOrder())) .compare(this, that); } {code} This is the same anti-pattern as OAK-12378 ({{PropertyTemplate.compareTo()}}), fixed by hoisting the comparator chain into a {{static final Comparator<MapEntry>}} field. This method is invoked via {{Arrays.sort}}/{{ComparableTimSort}} when persisting a {{MapRecord}} (see {{RecordWriters$MapLeafWriter.writeRecordContent}} and {{DefaultSegmentWriter$SegmentWriteOperation.writeMapLeaf}}), i.e. whenever a node's children are written as a persisted map — relevant to any node with enough children to use {{MapRecord}} rather than a flat list. h2. Evidence Found while profiling a bulk parallel-copy migration workload (JFR + async-profiler, ~793K nodes, 4 worker threads, Java assertions disabled to avoid unrelated noise). {{MapEntry.compareTo}} accounted for 14 of 31,263 total sampled leaf-frame weight in the async-profiler CPU capture, and 12 of 8,930 JFR execution samples with it as the top-of-stack frame — a smaller contributor than {{PropertyTemplate.compareTo}} in OAK-12378 (that recording was during compaction, a much more write-record-sorting-heavy workload), but the identical allocation pattern, confirmed via the following representative stack: {code:java} java.util.Arrays.sort(Object[]) java.util.ComparableTimSort.sort(...) java.util.ComparableTimSort.binarySort(...) org.apache.jackrabbit.oak.segment.MapEntry.compareTo(MapEntry) org.apache.jackrabbit.oak.segment.MapEntry.compareTo(Object) java.util.Comparator.thenComparing(...) java.util.Comparator.comparing(...) org.apache.jackrabbit.oak.segment.RecordWriters$MapLeafWriter.writeRecordContent(...) org.apache.jackrabbit.oak.segment.DefaultSegmentWriter$SegmentWriteOperation.writeMapLeaf(...) org.apache.jackrabbit.oak.segment.DefaultSegmentWriter$SegmentWriteOperation.writeMap(...) {code} Confirmed present verbatim (lines 150-155) on current {{apache/jackrabbit-oak}} trunk (commit {{44851487c5e4d0f9b9b46a40da79d9c78a3c83b9}}), not just an internal fork. h2. Suggested fix Same shape as the OAK-12378 fix: hoist the {{Comparator}} chain into a {{private static final Comparator<MapEntry>}} field built once, and have {{compareTo}} delegate to it. No behavior change; existing {{MapEntry}} tests should cover {{compareTo}} unchanged.

Restart reconfigured oak-run logging contexts to stop orphaned scanners
Description: Repeated oak-run commands in one JVM leave Logback's configuration scanner running after shutdown. The scanner can then create indexing.log under oak.workDir_IS_UNDEFINED in the module directory, causing Apache RAT to fail. h3. Cause LoggingInitializer reconfigures a LoggerContext stopped by an earlier command but does not restart it. With Logback 1.6.4, LoggerContext.stop() returns immediately when the context is already stopped, leaving the new file appender and scheduled configuration scanner active. When test-scoped system properties are restored and a watched configuration changes or disappears, the scanner reloads without oak.workDir and resolves the relative fallback directory. h3. Reproduction # Initialize indexing logging, then shut it down. # Initialize it again in the same JVM. The context remains stopped although a new scanner has been scheduled. # Shut down again. The scheduled scanner is not cancelled. # Restore/clear oak.workDir and modify the watched configuration. The exact stray log is created outside target. This was reproduced with the project's resolved Logback 1.6.4 dependencies, independent of cache maintenance changes. h3. Proposed fix and validation Restart the reconfigured logging context so shutdown closes the appender and cancels its scanner. Add deterministic regression tests for repeated initialization/shutdown, retain the external-configuration opt-out, and verify generated logging artifacts stay under test-scoped build output. Do not add RAT exclusions for the stray log. [Failing build on PR 3185|https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit-oak/actions/runs/37422282668/job/112134394437] h3. Regression introduction (verified) [Commit 50bde7adad3c8361447f5e06ce32413e8776d8e6|https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit-oak/commit/50bde7adad3c8361447f5e06ce32413e8776d8e6] (OAK-10339, PR #1343, 29 September 2026) upgraded SLF4J 1.7.36 / Logback 1.2.13 to SLF4J 2.0.20 / Logback 1.6.4. LoggingInitializer itself is unchanged across that commit. Logback 1.2.13 LoggerContext.stop() unconditionally resets the context, closes appenders and cancels scanning. Logback 1.6.4 returns immediately when the context is stopped. Oak's second initialization configures a stopped context but never starts it, exposing the missing lifecycle transition. This is independent of the cache maintenance changes in PR #3185. Controlled comparison using the same original Oak LoggingInitializer and two init/shutdown cycles: ||Dependencies||Context started after second init||Scanner cancelled after second shutdown|| |Logback 1.2.13 / SLF4J 1.7.36|false|true| |Logback 1.6.4 / SLF4J 2.0.20|false|false| |Logback 1.6.4 / SLF4J 2.0.20 with fix|true|true| h3. Validation Three regression tests fail before the production fix; all four new tests pass afterwards. The Java 17 oak-run-commons unit suite passes: 247 tests, zero failures/errors, one existing skip. Packaging and RAT pass with zero unapproved files. Tests use unique work directories under target, check scanner cancellation and file appender shutdown, and preserve the external logback.configurationFile opt-out.

Elasticsearch retains the built-in nodetype and uuid indexes, whose reindex counts also match; Lucene removes these indexes during setup. The Elasticsearch assertion therefore expects one result but receives three. Reproduced on unmodified trunk b062e3387d: ElasticFunctionIndexCommonTest#opFunctionConditionalPathQuery fails with [/oak:index/a, /oak:index/nodetype, /oak:index/uuid]. The same Lucene test passes. title: AzureDataStoreRegistrar ignores staging and minimum record length settings
Description: Azure datastore configuration can silently enable asynchronous uploads even when stagingSplitPercentage=0. This affects both SDK v8 and v12 through the OSGi registrar introduced in Oak 2.6.0. AzureDataStoreRegistrar returns DelegatingDataStore. AbstractDataStoreService applies PropertiesUtil.populate(ds, config, false), but the wrapper has no setters for stagingSplitPercentage, stagingPurgeInterval, stagingRetryInterval or minRecordLength. These settings are ignored; the active datastore retains its defaults, including 10% upload staging. Passing the configuration to setProperties does not populate these datastore fields. Reproduced with the released Oak 2.6.0 JAR: direct configuration applies stagingSplitPercentage=0, while configuration through the wrapper leaves it at 10 for both SDKs. Forwarding the four missing setters restores all tested values. The minRecordLength setter requires dispatch to the concrete AzureDataStore/AzureDataStoreV12 classes. Add these setters and regression tests that populate the wrapper configuration for both SDKs. Existing integration tests set stagingSplitPercentage directly on the concrete stores, bypassing the production configuration path. Introduced by OAK-12219, [PR #2989|https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit-oak/pull/2989], commit e33efd6156d3b74a18d3e9f9e0b4fcd8cde32086.

Oak-run check wrongly reports "No good revision found" when the corrupt path doesn't exist in older revisions
Description: When the newer revision has a corrupt node that was added after an older, consistent revision, check rejects the older revision too, because it re-tests the corrupt path there and treats the missing path as invalid. The result is a misleading {*}No good revision found{*}. *Example:* To explain the bug, here are the contents of the revisions: * Valid Revision ** Adds child nodes a, b, c, d, e, f with various properties (blobs included). * Invalid Revision ** Adds child node z with some blob properties and then corrupts the NODE record holding z. When oak-run check is run, it detects that the second revision is broken and marks the path /z as corrupt. It then continues with the first revision, which is valid. Before traversing an older revision, the checker first re-tests the corrupt paths found in newer revisions. /z does not exist in the first revision, and a missing path is counted as invalid. The valid revision is therefore rejected without being traversed, and the check ends with: Error while traversing /z: ...Segment reference out of bounds Path /z not found No good revision found Running check on the first revision alone gives Path / is consistent.

title: Oak-run indexing can miss entries with mongoParallelDump enabled

Very narrow includedPaths (restrictive MongoDB path) filtering makes this scenario more likely, because it can have long gaps between returned batches.

title: S3 accelerated presigned URLs use an unsupported regional endpoint
Description: S3 direct upload/download URLs use an unsupported hostname when transfer acceleration is enabled and no custom endpoint is configured. h3. Cause and impact {{Utils.createPresigner(..., true)}} sets an endpoint override from {{getEndPointUri}}. The endpoint builder returns {{s3-accelerate.<region>.amazonaws.com}}, producing an invalid accelerated URL instead of {{<bucket>.s3-accelerate.amazonaws.com}}. This affects accelerated direct binary access; ordinary non-accelerated access is outside this issue. Present on trunk at {{aeff1ea56039f5bfca6ec74995427d8e4991b0df}}: * [Presigner endpoint override|https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit-oak/blob/aeff1ea56039f5bfca6ec74995427d8e4991b0df/oak-blob-cloud/src/main/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/oak/blob/cloud/s3/Utils.java#L169-L182] * [Endpoint construction|https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit-oak/blob/aeff1ea56039f5bfca6ec74995427d8e4991b0df/oak-blob-cloud/src/main/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/oak/blob/cloud/s3/Utils.java#L365-L383] h3. Reproduction Build a presigner with static test credentials, a region such as {{us-east-1}}, acceleration requested, and no custom endpoint. Presign a GET or PUT for a DNS-compatible bucket and inspect the hostname. No live AWS call is needed to observe the malformed URL. h3. Expected behavior and fix Use the SDK acceleration configuration or the supported global acceleration endpoint. Keep the signing region configured separately and preserve non-accelerated/custom-endpoint behavior. Add regression coverage asserting the exact supported host for accelerated GET and PUT URLs, rather than only checking for the substring {{s3-accelerate}}. Update the existing endpoint-builder test that expects the regional acceleration hostname. [AWS Transfer Acceleration requirements|https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/transfer-acceleration.html] Related credential/presigner changes: OAK-12476.

title: S3Mock endpoint assumes Docker is reachable on JVM loopback
Description: S3Mock-backed tests can connect to the wrong host when Docker runs remotely or in a Docker-in-Docker environment. The helper always uses the JVM loopback address instead of the host reported by Testcontainers. h3. Cause and impact {{S3MockRule.getHttpEndpoint()}} returns {{http://127.0.0.1:}} plus the mapped port. That port is exposed on the Docker host, which need not be the JVM host. Container startup can succeed and {{S3EmulatorSupport.isAvailable()}} can return true, while subsequent metadata requests fail because they target the wrong address. Typical local Docker configurations may be unaffected. This is a test-infrastructure issue, not a production datastore defect. Present on trunk at {{aeff1ea56039f5bfca6ec74995427d8e4991b0df}}: [S3MockRule endpoint construction|https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit-oak/blob/aeff1ea56039f5bfca6ec74995427d8e4991b0df/oak-blob-cloud/src/test/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/oak/blob/cloud/s3/S3MockRule.java#L96-L107] h3. Reproduction Run an S3Mock-backed metadata test with a working remote Docker daemon or Docker-in-Docker setup where {{container.getHost()}} is not the JVM loopback address. Container startup succeeds, but the configured S3 endpoint still uses {{127.0.0.1}} and requests target the wrong host. h3. Expected behavior and fix Construct the endpoint using {{container.getHost()}} together with {{container.getMappedPort(HTTP_PORT)}}. Add focused regression coverage using a non-loopback container host and verify the resulting endpoint preserves that host and mapped port. Preserve local Docker behavior and the existing handling of unavailable Docker. [Testcontainers networking guidance|https://java.testcontainers.org/features/networking/] Related emulator infrastructure: OAK-12241.

Description: When an Oak Lucene index definition configures a function-based index (e.g. function = "first([sling:alias])") without also defining a separate property index on the underlying property (e.g. sling:alias), updates to that property on existing nodes are not detected during incremental or synchronous indexing. Root Cause: In IndexDefinition.java (lines 1395-1406): When a property definition has pd.function != null, it is added to functionRestrictions and "continue;" is called. It is never added to propDefns (which populates propConfigs). As a result: 1. indexingRule.isIndexed(propertyName) returns false for the property used by the function. 2. When the property is modified on an existing node, FulltextIndexEditor.propertyChanged() checks indexingRule.isIndexed(name). Since it returns false, propertiesChanged remains false. 3. In FulltextIndexEditor.leave(), the node is skipped and not re-indexed. Resolution / Workaround: Adding a dedicated property definition for the underlying property (e.g. name = "sling:alias", propertyIndex = true) alongside the function definition ensures indexingRule.isIndexed("sling:alias") returns true, allowing FulltextIndexEditor to detect changes on existing nodes and reindex the function value synchronously on commit. Automated Tests: Two unit tests demonstrating both the failure and resolution have been added to HybridIndexTest.java: 1. testSlingResourceResolverFunctionIndexAloneDoesNotDetectPropertyUpdate: Shows that when only the function is configured, updating sling:alias on existing nodes is not detected or re-indexed. 2. testSlingResourceResolverSyncIndex: Shows that declaring sling:alias as a property rule alongside the function index enables synchronous re-indexing on commit across multiple update phases. {code:java} @Test public void testSlingResourceResolverFunctionIndexAloneDoesNotDetectPropertyUpdate() throws Exception { Tree idx = root.getTree("/").getChild("oak:index").addChild("slingResourceResolver-funcOnly"); idx.setProperty("evaluatePathRestrictions", true, Type.BOOLEAN); idx.setProperty("includedPaths", List.of("/content"), Type.STRINGS); idx.setProperty("queryPaths", List.of("/content"), Type.STRINGS); Tree properties = ntBase.addChild("properties"); properties.setProperty(JcrConstants.JCR_PRIMARYTYPE, JcrConstants.NT_UNSTRUCTURED, Type.NAME); // ONLY function property definition, NO explicit sling:alias property definition Tree aliasProp = properties.addChild("alias"); aliasProp.setProperty(JcrConstants.JCR_PRIMARYTYPE, JcrConstants.NT_UNSTRUCTURED, Type.NAME); aliasProp.setProperty("name", "sling:alias", Type.STRING); aliasProp.setProperty("function", "first([sling:alias])", Type.STRING); aliasProp.setProperty("propertyIndex", true, Type.BOOLEAN); aliasProp.setProperty("ordered", true, Type.BOOLEAN); root.commit(); runAsyncIndex(); setTraversalEnabled(false); // 1. Initial creation of content: indexed because node is new (!before.exists()) Tree node1 = createPath("/content/node1"); node1.setProperty("sling:alias", List.of("alias1", "extra1"), Type.STRINGS); Tree node2 = createPath("/content/node2"); node2.setProperty("sling:alias", List.of("alias2", "extra2"), Type.STRINGS); root.commit(); String query = "select [jcr:path] from [nt:base] where isdescendantnode('/content') and first([sling:alias]) >= '' order by first([sling:alias])"; assertThat(explain(query), containsString("/oak:index/slingResourceResolver-funcOnly")); // Initial creation is queryable assertQuery(query, List.of("/content/node1", "/content/node2")); // 2. Update sling:alias on existing nodes node1.setProperty("sling:alias", List.of("aliasZ", "extra1"), Type.STRINGS); node2.setProperty("sling:alias", List.of("aliasA", "extra2"), Type.STRINGS); root.commit(); // Because sling:alias is not in propDefns, isIndexed("sling:alias") was false. // The update was NOT re-indexed on commit: the query still returns the old order [node1, node2] // rather than the updated order [node2 (aliasA), node1 (aliasZ)]. List<String> result = executeQuery(query, "JCR-SQL2"); assertEquals("Without sling:alias property definition, existing node property update is not detected", List.of("/content/node1", "/content/node2"), result); } @Test public void testSlingResourceResolverSyncIndexWithPropertyIndexFalse() throws Exception { runSlingResourceResolverSyncTest("slingResourceResolver-propIdxFalse", propAlias -> { propAlias.setProperty("propertyIndex", false, Type.BOOLEAN); }); } @Test public void testSlingResourceResolverSyncIndexWithIndexFalse() throws Exception { runSlingResourceResolverSyncTest("slingResourceResolver-indexFalse", propAlias -> { propAlias.setProperty("index", false, Type.BOOLEAN); }); } @Test public void testSlingResourceResolverSyncIndexWithPropertyIndexTrue() throws Exception { runSlingResourceResolverSyncTest("slingResourceResolver-propIdxTrue", propAlias -> { propAlias.setProperty("propertyIndex", true, Type.BOOLEAN); }); } private void runSlingResourceResolverSyncTest(String indexName, java.util.function.Consumer<Tree> propAliasConfigurator) throws Exception { Tree idx = root.getTree("/").getChild("oak:index").addChild(indexName); idx.setProperty(JcrConstants.JCR_PRIMARYTYPE, "oak:QueryIndexDefinition", Type.NAME); idx.setProperty("type", "lucene", Type.STRING); idx.setProperty("compatVersion", 2L, Type.LONG); idx.setProperty("async", List.of("async", "sync"), Type.STRINGS); idx.setProperty("evaluatePathRestrictions", true, Type.BOOLEAN); idx.setProperty("includedPaths", List.of("/content"), Type.STRINGS); idx.setProperty("queryPaths", List.of("/content"), Type.STRINGS); Only update alias in test (using array) node1.setProperty("sling:alias", List.of("alias5", "extra1"), Type.STRINGS); node2.setProperty("sling:alias", List.of("alias0", "extra2"), Type.STRINGS); node3.setProperty("sling:alias", List.of("alias4"), Type.STRINGS); // Commit updates root.commit(); // Query immediately after commit without any async indexing run // New order by first([sling:alias]): node2 (alias0), node3 (alias4), node1 (alias5) assertQuery(query, List.of("/content/node2", "/content/node3", "/content/node1")); // 3. title: Make IncrementalStoreTest independent of background write timing
Description: IncrementalStoreTest can export the initial content when it expects the final content, causing unrelated CI builds to fail. h3. Failure [GitHub Actions failure on PR 3268|https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit-oak/actions/runs/42075556392/job/127414676101?pr=3268]: testWithNoCompression fails in createFFS while checking the final flat file store. For example, /content/dam/2022/02 still has p1=v202202 instead of v202202-new, and newly added nodes are missing. h3. Cause The test uses setAsyncDelay(1) and opens separate read-only DocumentNodeStores immediately after committing content. Their root revision comes from persisted _lastRev values. If the writer has not flushed its pending background updates, the read-only store exports an older revision. Creating a checkpoint does not replace that required publication step. h3. Reproduction With MongoDB available, run mvn -pl oak-run -Dtest=IncrementalStoreTest#testWithNoCompression test. The ordinary run may pass. To reproduce deterministically, set the test builder asyncDelay to 0 and call runBackgroundOperations() after createBaseContent only. The final export then fails with the same initial-versus-final content mismatch as the linked CI job. h3. Fix Disable automatic background operations in this test and explicitly run the writer background operations after both base and incremental content commits, before creating the respective read-only stores. Retain all six compression/filter scenarios and their existing assertions. No production behavior changes. Related historical reports: OAK-11027 and OAK-11298 (both closed).

Full GC commit-root cleanup loses cross-cluster child visibility
Description: Full GC can remove commit metadata still needed to reconstruct a node's child view. With embedded verification enabled, cleanup is rejected even though current user-property values are unchanged. Without verification, the same cleanup can hide children. h3. Affected behavior Reproduced with oak-run 1.84.0 and the unmodified 2.8.0 release using Full GC mode 6 (ORPHANS_EMPTYPROPS_KEEP_ONE_ALL_PROPS), dryRun=true and verify=true. Also reproduced by a synthetic regression on trunk at {{3e918022228f81da0cd740dfa7cd677cd7ba4c55}}. The warning is {{removeGarbage.verify : verifyViaTraversedState failed}}. Candidate revision counts are reported, but the rejected document is not updated. h3. Cause {{NodeDocument.createLastRevs()}} derives per-cluster modification revisions from both {{_lastRev}} and local {{_revisions}}/{{_commitRoot}} metadata. {{collectUnusedInternalPropertyRevisions()}} can remove a cluster's latest committed {{_commitRoot}} entry when no retained property value references it. If persisted {{_lastRev}} does not cover that cluster's changes, the computed {{DocumentNodeState.getLastRevision()}} vector regresses and descendant reads lose visibility. Dry-run instrumentation confirmed that the original document reconstructed directly matches traversal. Simulated cleanup leaves the current property unchanged but changes the computed revision vector and child enumeration. Restoring only {{_commitRoot}} entries on an in-memory copy restores full state equality, without restoring obsolete user-property history. h3. Synthetic reproduction # Share a fresh {{MemoryDocumentStore}} between {{DocumentNodeStore}} cluster IDs 1 and 2, using a virtual clock and disabled background scheduling. # From cluster 1, create {{/parent}} and {{/other}} in one commit. # From cluster 1, update a property on both nodes and create {{/parent/firstChild}}. Commit another property update on both nodes. Updating both paths ensures commit roots reside on the repository root rather than the parent. # Flush background operations and synchronize cluster 2. From cluster 2, overwrite the same property on both nodes and create {{/parent/secondChild}}. Flush and synchronize cluster 1. # On the synthetic parent document only, remove cluster 1's persisted {{_lastRev}} map entry. Its committed {{_commitRoot}} history still supplies that cluster's latest revision, so both children remain visible before GC. # Add a newer, uncommitted property/commit-root entry to exercise skipping uncommitted revisions when determining what metadata to retain. # Advance the clock by two hours. Run Full GC mode 6 with a one-hour retention window, scoped to {{/parent}}. # With verification enabled, assert cleanup is accepted and obsolete property history is pruned. Repeat as a verified dry-run. With verification disabled, assert both children, full node-state equality, and the original computed revision vector remain intact. Before the fix, all three configurations fail: normal and dry-run verification reject the parent, while unverified cleanup regresses the revision vector and child view. h3. Fix and regression The local fix retains the newest committed {{_commitRoot}} entry per cluster when collecting unused internal property revisions. Older entries remain eligible for collection; a newer uncommitted entry does not replace the required committed one. No {{_lastRev}} rewrite or verification bypass is introduced. {{FullGCRevisionRetentionTest}} contains the three parameterized synthetic cases. Run with: {code} mvn -pl oak-store-document -Dtest=FullGCRevisionRetentionTest test {code} No production document, identifiers, connection details, or raw data are included.

title: Revision GC never completes on MongoDB: MongoVersionGCSupport.identifyGarbage is exponential in number of sweep revisions
Description: *Context.* Our application embeds Oak 2.8.0 (DocumentNodeStore on MongoDB, outside OSGi) and runs on Kubernetes. Since nothing schedules revision GC outside OSGi, it had never run; we introduced a daily maintenance job that runs blob GC (MarkSweepGarbageCollector) and then revision GC (VersionGarbageCollector.gc(24h)), guarded by a cluster-wide lock so that it runs on one instance at a time. Every new pod gets a new cluster id, so over months of deployments the root document accumulated 153 entries in _sweepRev (only 1 active cluster node). *Symptom.* On the first runs blob GC completed in a couple of minutes, but revision GC never did: runs were still going after 1h51m and 12h43m, one core at 100% and no Mongo activity, until a deployment restarted the process. Meanwhile the lock stayed held and other maintenance tasks failed. The "versionGC" settings document was never created, i.e. no iteration ever completed, although the repository is small (~64k documents, 1,063 split documents). The official oak-run 2.8.0 "revisions collect" on a copy of the database behaves the same: --timeLimit has no effect and SIGTERM does not stop it. Thread dumps always show 260+ nested LazyIteratorChain frames: {code:java} org.apache.commons.collections4.iterators.LazyIteratorChain.updateCurrentIterator(LazyIteratorChain.java:149) org.apache.commons.collections4.iterators.LazyIteratorChain.hasNext(LazyIteratorChain.java:84) org.apache.commons.collections4.iterators.LazyIteratorChain.hasNext(LazyIteratorChain.java:86) ... (262-267 nested LazyIteratorChain frames) org.apache.jackrabbit.oak.plugins.document.SplitDocumentCleanUp.disconnect(SplitDocumentCleanUp.java:62) org.apache.jackrabbit.oak.plugins.document.VersionGCSupport.deleteSplitDocuments(VersionGCSupport.java:165) org.apache.jackrabbit.oak.plugins.document.VersionGarbageCollector$GCJob.collectSplitDocuments(VersionGarbageCollector.java:1093) {code} *Cause.* Since OAK-11451 (Guava removal, 1.78.0; 1.76.0 is not affected), MongoVersionGCSupport.identifyGarbage() chains the results of its queries in a loop: {code:java} Iterable<NodeDocument> allResults = emptyList(); for (Bson query : queries) { ... allResults = IterableUtils.chainedIterable(allResults, iterable); } {code} When DEFAULT_NO_BRANCH is collected, createQueries() returns one query per sweep revision entry plus one final query, so the chain is nested once per cluster id. Guava's Iterables.concat flattened nested concatenations; commons-collections4 LazyIteratorChain.hasNext() calls hasNext() twice on the nested iterator, so an element returned by the first queries costs ~2^(N+1) hasNext() calls (known issue COLLECTIONS-722). In this repository the DEFAULT_NO_BRANCH split documents belong to low cluster ids, i.e. to the most deeply nested queries. *Fix.* Collect the per-query iterables in a list and chain them once: {code:java} List<Iterable<NodeDocument>> results = new ArrayList<>(queries.size()); for (Bson query : queries) { ... results.add(iterable); } return IterableUtils.chainedIterable(results); {code} *Verification.* * Patched oak-run 2.8.0, same command and data: GC completes in 4.1 s (local copy) / 4.0 min (original database, --delay 0.5) with splitDocGCCount=986, intermediateSplitDocGCCount=55; repository content verified unchanged. * Synthetic reproduction (MongoDB, N cluster ids each with a DEFAULT_NO_BRANCH split document): ||N||stock 2.8.0||patched|| |20|0.58 s|< 0.5 s| |26|12.6 s|< 0.5 s| |28|50.3 s|< 0.5 s| |30|timeout (180 s)|< 0.5 s| |153|does not complete|1.4 s| * Regression test: MongoRevisionGCTest#identifyGarbageWithManySweepRevisions (40 sweep revisions, 1 DEFAULT_NO_BRANCH document) times out after 30 s without the fix and passes with it. No other occurrence of the "x = chainedIterable(x, ...)" pattern exists in the code base.

SegmentTarReader cannot distinguish a missing from a corrupt binary references entry
Description: {{SegmentArchiveReader.getBinaryReferences()}} may return {{null}} when an archive has no binary references. The remote readers (Azure, AWS) do that when the {{.brf}} file is missing. {{SegmentTarReader.getBinaryReferences()}} is declared {{{}@NotNull{}}}. It doesn't check whether the archive has a {{.brf}} entry; it computes where the entry should end from the sizes of the index and graph entries and reads from there. When the entry is missing (e.g. a TAR archive written by {{SegmentStoreMigrator}} before OAK-12516), it reads the end of the last segment and fails with: {noformat} java.io.IOException: org.apache.jackrabbit.oak.segment.file.tar.binaries.InvalidBinaryReferencesIndexException: Unrecognized magic number {noformat} A {{.brf}} entry with a corrupt magic number fails with the same exception, so callers can't tell a missing entry from a corrupt one. The archive layout distinguishes the two cases. After the segments, a TAR archive contains the {{{}.brf{}}}, {{.gph}} and {{.idx}} entries, in this order, each with a header containing its name.

title: Missing binary references (.brf) of segment archives are lost by data store GC, compaction cleanup and SegmentStoreMigrator
Description: When an archive of a segment store has no binary references entry ({{.brf}}), or the entry can't be read, {{TarReader.getBinaryReferences()}} and {{SegmentArchiveReader.getBinaryReferences()}} return {{null}} (see OAK-12527). The operations that use the binary references of an archive then lose them: * *Data store GC*: {{TarReader.collectBlobReferences}} returns without reporting any reference for that archive. The mark phase misses the binaries referenced only from it, and the sweep can delete binaries that are still in use. * *Compaction cleanup*: when {{TarReader.sweep}} rewrites such an archive, it copies no binary references, and {{TarWriter}} writes an empty {{.brf}} into the new archive. The references are lost permanently, and later data store GC runs read the empty entry without any warning. * *Segment store migration*: {{SegmentStoreMigrator}} (Azure) and {{AwsSegmentStoreMigrator}} skip the missing binary references silently, and the archive is migrated without a {{.brf}} entry. When the target is a TAR store, reading the binary references of that archive failed with the following error, which looks like data corruption although the segments are intact: {noformat} java.io.IOException: org.apache.jackrabbit.oak.segment.file.tar.binaries.InvalidBinaryReferencesIndexException: Unrecognized magic number at org.apache.jackrabbit.oak.segment.file.tar.SegmentTarReader.getBinaryReferences(SegmentTarReader.java:147) {noformat} Since OAK-12527 the missing entry is reported as {{null}}, so the migrated archive is affected by the data store GC and cleanup problems above. An archive can have no usable {{.brf}} when: * a remote archive (Azure, AWS) is still open, or the Oak process terminated before closing it, because its binary references are written only when it is closed; * a TAR archive was written without it, e.g. by {{SegmentStoreMigrator}} from such a remote archive; * the entry is corrupt. TAR recovery doesn't cover this case, because it only runs for archives without a valid index. *Fix*: recover the binary references from the segments of the archive with the store's {{TarRecovery}} when the {{.brf}} entry is missing or can't be read: * data store GC collects the recovered references; * compaction cleanup writes the recovered references of the remaining segments into the rewritten archive; * the migrators recover them with a read-only store of the source, so the source is never modified, and always write a {{.brf}} into the target archive.

title: faces.util.chain behavior changed
Description: Given the following generated HTML, an alert will occur. If you click OK, it will perform an action on a backing bean. However, if you cancel, it should not. {code:java} <input type="submit" value="Test" onclick="return faces.util.chain(this, event,function(event){return confirm('Please Confirm');});">{code} On Faces 3.0, if cancel is pressed, then the backing bean is not invoked. On Faces 4.0, however, pressing cancel *does* invoke the bean. Faces 3.0: jsf.util.chain snippet: {noformat} if (FUNC == typeof arguments[cnt]) { ret = arguments[cnt].call(source, event); } else { //either a function or a string can be passed in case of a string we have to wrap it into another function ret = new Function("event", arguments[cnt]).call(source, event); } //now if one function returns false in between we stop the execution of the cycle //here, note we do a strong comparison here to avoid constructs like 'false' or null triggering if (ret === false /*undefined check implicitly done here by using a strong compare*/) { return false; } }{noformat} Faces 4.0: {noformat} function chain(source, event, ...funcs) { // we can use our lazy stream each functionality to run our chain here. // by passing a boolean as return value into the onElem call // we can stop early at the first false, just like the spec requests let ret; funcs.every(func => { let returnVal = resolveAndExecute(source, event, func); if (returnVal !== false) { ret = returnVal; } return returnVal !== false; }); return ret; }{noformat} It looks like conditions changed here? "ret === false" became "returnVal !== false" ? If cancel is pressed, false is returned, which means the chain function returns false in 3.0. In faces 4.0, ret is never set (due to the new condition), so undefined (ret) is returned now instead.

title: ajax event listener looses 'source' in 'success' event
Description: I'm adding an event listener for the ajax events. I do this by calling `faces.ajax.addOnEvent(onEventFunction)` and I expect all forwarded events to have the 'source' value set to the original source that triggered the ajax flow. But this does not seem to work when switching to a different page. It works fine when the view stays on the same page. This used to work in 2.3.x versions and is needed by RichFaces. See [https://github.com/MilovdZee/myfaces-minimal-test] for an example of this behaviour. {code:java} function onEventFunction(data) { console.log(data); } faces.ajax.addOnEvent(onEventFunction);{code} And then in the xhtml of page 1: {code:java} <h:commandLink id="button" value="to page 2" action="#{pageSwitcherBean.toPage2()}"> <f:ajax/> </h:commandLink> {code} A plain commandbutton has no issue and the source is preserved in all statusses: {code:java} <h:commandButton id="button2" value="delay" actionListener="#{pageSwitcherBean.toPage2()}"> <f:ajax/> </h:commandButton> {code} My expectation is that this has to do with the render of the elements. The source dom element disappears due to the fresh rendering of the page. And this also means that it does not sound that weird that the source is null. The element is gone anyway and so the meaning is minimal. But it very much looks like it used to be there. For reference I also added the same functionality with myfaces 2.3.11. title: Update the typescript compiler and build codebase to Typescript 6.0
Description: While functionally nothing should change, typescript 6 is an important stepping stone towards Typescript 7 which will be a Rust rewrite of the entire compiler codebase. With it there will be some breaking changes regarding module support which TS 6 already implements. The bundling now is offloaded into a separate bundler via the bundler directive and webpack is our bundler and has been quite a while. With the the node module support will get breaking changes in the build process. I have already prepared a new TS6 enabled version in my github project and this needs to be upstreamed now into myfaces, however here also some changes need to be performed on the setup for the build regarding the module resolution changes! Also several things have been fixed and AI has been introduced in my private workflow on the downstram project Updated to the latest version of the codebase * Websocket error and recovery lifecycle is now fixed and according to the spec (there were several minor issues regarding recovery and event callback) * In some core classes the readability has been improved * 404 now is properly reported, the old code reported an "illegal XML Exception" instead * File Upload had an explicit content type set, which can bring the browser into an unstable state (this is not set by the browser) - the browser now sets the content type for file upload itself, verified on a browser that this works! * Around 100 tests added which fortify now the push lifecycle and cover now up until now uncovered code! * Ai disclaimers and markers added for code added and touched by AI toolings to be in accordance with the ASF guidelies Full detailed changelist can be found in the downstream project: [https://github.com/werpu/jsfs_js_ts]

title: Spec change faces.d.ts must be provided
Description: [https://github.com/jakartaee/faces/issues/1598#issuecomment-4490784716] As it seems mojarra also now has improved their typescript typescript, and there is a spec improvement going underway that a faces.d.ts file must be provided so that the js codebase can be used within typescript. We need to add this functionality. First I need to do the generation of this file or providing it manually within the downstram project on github and then it will need to be integrated in myfaces. Not sure if we need to present that file on request, I doubt it because the d.ts files are plain files provided so that you can link javascript into typescript code without losing the type information on the apis! So I guess just providing it is enough. Still the preferred way probably for projects would be anyway just use the plain typescript files but, the d.ts file is valid and needs to be at least packaged in!

title: "Maximum call stack size exceeded" when AJAX updating large DOM in Chromium based browsers

This is caused by an issue that Chromium (or more specifically V8) is aware of but don't care to fix, the earliest report I could find is from 2022: [https://issues.chromium.org/issues/41467953] . The issue is reproducible with the following xhtml, which creates 100,000 empty divs (it breaks somewhere between 60k and 70k). I believe the only thing that matters is the total number of elements in the DOM. {noformat}

title: Move from hard-code menu location to parameterized
Description: Customization is a key aspect of the OFBiz (Open For Business) platform, providing businesses with a robust and adaptable base to customize their enterprise software solutions according to their unique operational requirements. The *Menus.xml file of a component, essential for designing user interfaces that are both intuitive and tailored to the specific roles and tasks of its users, plays a significant role in this context, as referenced within screen widgets and Freemarker templates. However, as customizations and the project's source code evolve over time, the likelihood of encountering merge conflicts increases significantly, especially when attempting to incorporate customizations alongside ongoing bug fixes and enhancements from the project. To improve the appeal of OFbiz and the developer experience, it is recommended to shift from fixed menu locations to a parameterized approach in our components and plugins. This change would enable developers to more seamlessly incorporate a 'custom' menu, facilitating the integration of project updates.

title: Prevent possible file race conditions with SecuredUpload class
Description: While trying to upload PDF files I found a possible file race conditions in DataServices::createFileMethod and DataServices::updateFileMethod The same could exist in several places in ImageManagementServices and ProductServices classes

title: ‎SecuredUpload‎::checkMaxLinesLength put in a regression for PDF files
Description: As commented at [https://s.apache.org/wpkuj,] while working on OFBIZ-12926 I realised that checkMaxLinesLength put in a possible regression for PDF files. As a summary: we can't use checkMaxLinesLength for PDF files because they may contain several CharSet encodings. Hence no possibility to use Files::readAllLines that needs a sole CharSet. So we need to bypass this check.

title: Modal title not supported on hyperlink in form fields
Description: Hyperlinks elements can trigger the opening of a modal window (link-type="layered-modal"). OFBiz uses jQuery UI Dialog to achieve this, and parameters for this library are passed through a set of data-dialog-* ** attributes on the "a" tag, in "HtmlFormMacroLibrary::makeHyperlinkString" Freemarker macro. Then in OfbizUtil.js, links that should open modals are processed : data-dialog-* are used to configure jQueryUI Dialog module. In OfbizUtil.js, data-dialog-text attribute is used to set the title of the modal (text in the colored top bar). The value of this attribute is set using the "text" parameter in "makeHyperlinkString" macro. However, this macro does not declare a "text" parameter in its signature, and HtmlMacroFormRenderer::makeHyperlinkString does not support it. As a result, we cannot set the modal title when using a `hyperlink` tag with a `text` attribute in a form (although the code indicates otherwise). !image-2024-03-14-08-58-13-835.png!

title: Use Development Containers as development environments with necessary build tools already available
Description: Development Containers are becoming a popular method of ensuring a container-based development environment has all the tools needed by a developer to work on a project. Development Containers ([https://containers.dev/)] depend on the developer's host system running a container runtime, such as Docker. They are supported in IntelliJ and VS Code. Inclusion of a Development Container configuration in the ofbiz-framework sources will allow new developers to open their IDE with all development tools - such as the correct version of Java SDK - already in place. This should improve the on-boarding experience for new developers. Outside of IDE integration, tools such as DevPod can be used to create and run Development Containers targeting a project. Users can then SSH into the container and carry out development tasks such as gradle builds. This might be an integration point for IDEs that do not currently have support Development Containers, such as Eclipse. Further reading: [https://blog.jetbrains.com/idea/2024/07/using-dev-containers-in-jetbrains-ides-part-1/] [https://github.com/JetBrains/devcontainers-examples] [https://containers.dev/]

title: String to numeric conversion does not support non-breaking spaces
Description: When submitting a form with numeric values, OFBiz uses a text input (`<input type="text"/>`), so all characters (entered by hand or pasted) are allowed in the input. On form's submission, for numeric fields, the string is parsed using `java.text.NumberFormat` class (parse method), using a number instance formatter. This formatter does not supports non-breaking spaces ('\u00A0', '\u202F', '\u2007'), and characters after a non-breaking space are ignored : !image-2024-11-05-11-01-13-030.png|width=337,height=153! This can lead to a situation where a visually correct form stores wrong values : [^Peek 05-11-2024 10-59.mp4] One of our client reported this situation while pasting values from external tools. Some values where truncated, because the external tool used non-breaking spaces when displaying values.

title: Bug persisting uploaded files with service attachUploadToDataResource

There is a boolean property "forceLocal" which is filled by the method UtilProperties.getPropertyAsValue. This method returns a string instead of a boolean which causes Groovy to interpret this value as "true" even if you configure that property to be "false". You can work around this problem by using an empty string in your properties when you want this boolean to be "false". A solution would be to use UtilProperties.getPropertyAsBoolean instead.
